title: Introduce atomic tfstate lease rotation and GPU nodepool tiler module
author: Maya Singh
release_notes: Adds an atomic tfstate lease rotation operator and a GPU nodepool tiler module to improve allocation stability and enable zero-downtime tfstate migration for private deployments.
description: Context and motivation: Private deployments require frequent state boundary adjustments (tenant split/merge, subnet reallocation) and safer GPU nodepool topology changes. Existing tfstate migrations are brittle when multiple controllers attempt to move locks or reassign subnet leases concurrently; we observed a customer incident where concurrent tf apply led to partial state updates and GPU pools losing affinity (INC-2026-02). This PR introduces two coordinated Terraform modules plus an operator helper: (1) tfstate-lease-rotator - an idempotent, atomic lease rotation pattern for tfstate backends that enables safe handoff of state ownership between control plane instances; (2) gpu-nodepool-tiler - a lightweight module that converts a desired GPU nodepool topology into per-AZ/tenant tiling claims and reconciliation hooks; and (3) network-alloc-policy - policy bits and helpers to ensure subnet claim ordering during rollout. Design summary: - A lease rotation is implemented by a short-lived, versioned mutex key in the tfstate backend with monotonic generation tags so rotations are compare-and-swap. Rotation is guarded by a preflight check that validates no outstanding apply sessions and drains the nodepool controller for 30s. - The tiler module expresses a tiling plan using a small CRD-compatible map (tiling_count, az_preference, gpu_profile). The module emits outputs for per-tenant subnet-claim resources and an optional migration path that creates shadow nodepools and migrates workloads via cordon/drain + instance replacement. - The network-alloc-policy adds ordering constraints and a reversible annotation schema so rollbacks can be performed without manual tfstate surgery. Migration plan and operator interplay: - Phase 1 (dry-run): rollout tiler in dry-run mode to produce tiling plan and diffs; no resources are created. - Phase 2 (prepare): create shadow nodepools + lease-rotator campaign (lock-rotate -> snapshot -> rotate -> unlock) to transfer temporary write authority to the migration controller. - Phase 3 (apply): apply tiler-created subnet claims and nodepool replacements while tfstate is under rotation lock; the operator watches and verifies nodepool health. - Phase 4 (finalize): rotate lease back to normal control plane and remove shadows. Rollback: the tiler preserves tombstone annotations to allow automatic rollback of the last commit; lease-rotator will detect partial rotations and revert to the previous generation if a healthcheck fails. Checklist: - [x] Add tf modules: tfstate-lease-rotator, gpu-nodepool-tiler, network-alloc-policy. - [x] Add unit tests for rotation CAS and tiler plan generator. - [x] Add e2e migration harness (simulated multi-controller tf apply). - [x] Add docs: design doc and migration runbook. - [x] Add Helm chart values mapping for private-installer to wire new modules. Compatibility and constraints: - Works with S3/GS/GCS backends that support object versioning; when backend lacks strong versioning, rotator will fall back to a conservative single-writer window but emits warnings. - The tiler requires nodepool replacement capability in the installer (supported by private-installer >= v0.21). Security considerations: lease-rotator operations require iam:PutObject/Lock and KMS decrypt for snapshotting; new IAM role module templates included. Testing & validation: local unit tests (+go test) for rotator logic, Terraform validate for modules, integration test in perf-canary that simulates concurrent applies (included). See CI summary below. Known limitations: very large fleets (>10k GPUs across regions) will prolong drain windows; future work: incremental tiling and soft-rebalance. Related: ENG-8724 design doc (link: https://linear.app/redwood/issue/ENG-8724/tfstate-lease-rotation-design).

review_comments: Diego Alvarez: Can we avoid snapshotting full tfstate for large buckets? Suggest incremental diff and object tagging.
Maya Singh (reply): Implemented incremental snapshot in d9e1f35 and added object tagging for easier rollbacks.
Priya Nair: Need clearer IAM least-privilege template for rotator. Also confirm KMS usage in docs.

Samir Patel: CI flaky on integration harness - observed timeout on simulated drain; increased default wait and added retry. Approved after fix.
testing_summary: Unit: rotator CAS tests (100% coverage for CAS paths), tiler plan generator unit tests. Integration: perf-canary scenario simulated two controllers running concurrent applies; rotation prevented conflict and tiler applied without resource conflicts. E2E run in staging passed with a small private-deploy cluster. CI runs: rotator-unit.yml -> pass, tiler-integration.yml -> pass after one re-run.
notes_for_ops: When running migration in customer environments: ensure private-installer version >= v0.21, backup tfstate snapshot locally before initiating rotation, monitor nodepool replacement progress and have rollback window configured. Use --var=tiler_dry_run=true to preview plans.
changelog_entry: Added tfstate-lease-rotator (atomic lease rotation), gpu-nodepool-tiler (topology -> claims mapping), network-alloc-policy helpers. Improves safety of tfstate migrations and GPU nodepool topology changes for private deployments.
